content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes; model reacts too aggressively to recent highs.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model underestimates persistence of upward trends.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10–15 days; later days show less error but still overestimated.
- Model fails to capture gradual price consolidation after spikes; assumes volatility fades too quickly.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic, especially when recent history shows volatility.
